symbols.note: copied from `gatekit symbols system <name> --dll dx11 --full` (addresses are bg3_dx11.exe; the Toolkit's own methods without an address were not found in the game binary and are listed with address null; the per-frame update address is not printed for bg3_dx11.exe by this command, it was found by reading the factory in pseudo-code). Parsed by script from the command output, not retyped.
symbols.limits: reads/writes: the component views in the parameters of the system's exported methods. uses: the component operations (add, remove, get, has) its per-frame update performs through the engine's out-of-line helpers, itself or in a function it calls (depth 2), with the call site; kind index: a matched method reads the type's index and the operation is not known. Not listed: operations the compiler inlined, those deeper than depth 2, and what a method that is not the update does (e.g. a SystemLoad) - read its pseudo-code; an empty writes list is not "writes nothing".

does.text: Adds and removes esv::combat::CanStartCombatComponent. The update runs three functions over one scratch map from entity to a number: the first two walk queries and put 0 or 1 against entities, the third adds the component (one byte, zeroed) to the entities marked 0 and removes it from those marked 1. The queries the first two walk are of the modified kind (QueryTypeModifiedTag), so they look at entities whose watched components changed; which components they watch was not identified.
does.evidence: bg3_dx11.exe factory 0x234BC20 (stores entry 0x238F290) -> update 0x3229EB0 -> 0x3228D30 and 0x3229520 (write 0 or 1 into the map), 0x3229D10 (adds CanStartCombatComponent on 0, removes it on 1). Read as pseudo-code.

unknown: What decides 0 versus 1 for an entity. The marking functions test storage-state bits of queries whose component lists were not named in the pseudo-code, so the 0/1 is not tied to a gameplay condition.
Which components the modified queries watch; the method signature lists character, combat participant and item, but the queries were not matched to them.
What having the component means for combat; only that 0 adds it and 1 removes it is read.
sure: no: the mark-then-add/remove structure is read from the code; the condition behind the marks is not understood
